land.text: the Bahmani heartland around Bidar, the Bahmani capital since 1429, and the eastern (Telangana) lands that Cliopatria draws inside Bidar to 1518

predecessors.note: Qasim Barid I 'in 1492 assumed de facto control of state affairs of the Bahmani Sultanate'; the Bahmani kings stayed on as puppets until 1527.

land.text: the whole of Bidar, 'annexed to Bijapur sultanate' after the defeat of Amir Barid III in 1619

successors.note: Cliopatria's Bijapur shape of 1619 contains 125 of the 126 Bidar cells (the other cell falls to Ahmadnagar's shape).

capitals.name: Bidar
capitals.note: The Bahmani capital since 1429 ('Following the establishment of Bidar as capital of the sultanate in 1429', Bahmani page); the Barid Shahi seat to the annexation of 1619.

rulers.name: Qasim Barid I
rulers.note: Table reign from 1489; the text dates his de facto control of the Bahmani state to 1492. Founder of the sultanate (1492).

rulers.name: Amir Barid I
rulers.note: Became 'practically independent' in 1527 when the last Bahmani king fled to Bidar; 'he never assumed any royal title'.

rulers.name: Ali Barid Shah I
rulers.note: 'The first to assume the royal title of Shah'; joined the Deccan sultans at Talikota in January 1565.

rulers.name: Ali Barid Shah II
rulers.note: Infant son of Qasim Barid II; succeeded in 1591.

rulers.name: Amir Barid Shah II
rulers.note: Overthrown in 1601 by a relative, Mirza Ali Barid.

rulers.name: Amir Barid Shah III
rulers.note: Fought the Mughals in 1616 under Malik Ambar; defeated by Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur in 1619.

keyframe_review.note: 63,693 km2 for 1492-1518; the page gives no extent and no area, and says only that Qasim Barid I took control of the Bahmani state in 1492. The shape includes about 145 cells (some 36,700 km2) in the east, the Telangana lands that Golconda takes in 1518-1519; no page opened divides the Bahmani provinces among the successors, so the shape stands as Cliopatria's partition of the Bahmani 1491 outline (1,632 cells): Ahmadnagar 309, Berar 282, Bijapur 482, Bidar 249.

26,342 km2 for 1519-1520 after the eastern Telangana lands pass to Golconda (Cliopatria's Golconda row begins 1519; the Qutb Shahi and Bahmani pages date Golconda to 1518). One cell is gained at the Berar edge (page silent).

32,231 km2 from 1521: 21 cells (about 5,300 km2) of the southern frontier gained, 14 from Vijayanagara's and 6 from Bijapur's 1520 shapes. No page opened dates a Bidar gain in the south (the Bidar page has no dated event between 1492 and 1527); kept as Cliopatria draws it.
A one-cell edge revision (about 250 km2) with no page behind it; shape kept.
The one cell is restored; boundary noise, no event.
One cell again removed; boundary noise, no event. The Bidar page records no territorial change in this span (Ali Barid Shah I died in 1580, Ibrahim Barid succeeded).

Identical to the 1579 shape. Cliopatria ends the row in 1618; the page's infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1619' and 'In 1619, he was defeated by the Bijapur sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II. Bidar was annexed to Bijapur sultanate.' Cliopatria's Bijapur shape already contains Bidar from 1619, so the Bidar shape should be dropped after 1618 and the dissolve event (1619) is the caption.

region.text: Bidar and the Bahmani heartland under Qasim Barid I

ledger.note: 1492: Qasim Barid I takes control of the Bahmani state at Bidar and founds the Barid Shahi line. 'The sultanate was founded in 1492 by Qasim Barid I'; he 'in 1492 assumed de facto control of state affairs of the Bahmani Sultanate' under Mahmud Shah Bahmani II. The Bahmani page: 'Qasim Barid I in 1492 saw the end of any real Bahmani power.' (The reign table starts his rule in 1489.)

region.text: the eastern lands of Cliopatria's Bidar shape (about 145 cells) that belong to Golconda from 1519

ledger.note: 1518-1519: the eastern lands pass to the new sultanate of Golconda. The Bahmani page dates Golconda to 1518 ('the last independent sultanate, Golkonda, in 1518') and the Quli Qutb Shah page gives his reign from 7 December 1518, but no page opened says which Bahmani province Golconda took; the land is the strip that Cliopatria moves from Bidar's 1518 shape to Golconda's 1519 shape.

region.text: the southern strip added to Bidar's shape in 1521

ledger.note: 1521: Bidar's southern frontier moves south. Cliopatria adds 21 cells in 1521 (14 from Vijayanagara, 6 from Bijapur); no page opened dates or explains it.

1527: the Bahmani state formally ends at Bidar. 'When the last Bahmani ruler Kalimullah fled to Bidar in 1527, Amir Barid I became practically independent, as his de jure suzerain's state ceased to exist. However, he never assumed any royal title.' The Bahmani page: 'the kingdom formally dissolved in 1527' after four puppet kings under Amir Barid I.
1542: Ali Barid Shah I is the first Barid to take the royal title of Shah, making Bidar a kingdom in name as well as fact.

region.text: the whole Barid Shahi territory around Bidar

ledger.note: 1619: Bijapur conquers Bidar. 'In 1619, he [Amir Barid III] was defeated by the Bijapur sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II. Bidar was annexed to Bijapur sultanate.' The Adil Shahi page: 'The following year [after 1618], Bijapur conquered the neighbouring Bidar Sultanate.'
1619: the Barid Shahi sultanate ends; Bidar is annexed to Bijapur (infobox 'Disestablished: 1619').

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: Victory of the Deccan sultanates; Rama Raya killed (23 January 1565) and Vijayanagara plundered. The page gives no territorial transfer to Bidar.
wars.note: 'Ali Barid Shah I of Bidar' is one of the four sultans who convened to attack Aliya Rama Raya; the Bidar page says he 'joined the other Deccan sultans in the Battle of Talikota against the Vijayanagar Empire in January 1565'.

wars.name: Bijapur conquest of Bidar

zones.text: Bidar, annexed by Ibrahim Adil Shah II

wars.outcome: Bijapur victory: Amir Barid III is defeated and Bidar is annexed to Bijapur.
wars.note: The Bidar page gives no campaign dates beyond 1619; Amir Barid III had 'fought against the Mughals in 1616 under the leadership of Malik Ambar'.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary survey or treaty line for Bidar; the frontiers with Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar are Cliopatria's approximations.

sources.title: Bidar Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, founding in 1492, Bidar as capital, rulers 1489-1619, Talikota, the 1619 annexation by Bijapur; no area figure.

sources.title: Bahmani Sultanate
sources.note: Bahmani break-up: Golconda 1518, dissolution 1527, Bidar capital since 1429, puppet kings under Amir Barid I.

sources.title: Battle of Talikota
sources.note: Bidar among the four sultanates at Talikota, 23 January 1565; no territorial transfers listed.

sources.title: Adil Shahi dynasty
sources.note: The 1619 conquest of Bidar by Bijapur ('The following year, Bijapur conquered the neighbouring Bidar Sultanate'); Bijapur's 1529 invasion of Bidar.

sources.title: Quli Qutb Shah
sources.note: Golconda's first sultan reigned from 7 December 1518 (dates the loss of Bidar's eastern lands).

notes: Bidar (7 Cliopatria shapes, 1492-1618): the page has few dated events and says nothing about extent, so the shapes are kept (verdict ok) except for the end year (1619 per the page; Cliopatria's Bijapur shape holds Bidar from 1619). The 1519 shrinkage (145 cells to Golconda) is Cliopatria's partition of the Bahmani lands; no page opened says how the provinces were divided (the Bahmani page lists no division). Bijapur's invasion of Bidar in 1529 (Adil Shahi page: 'Ismail invaded the territory of Amir Barid I of Bidar in 1529, besieging his capital') changed no border. The Qasim Barid I reign table begins 1489 but the text dates his control to 1492; the dossier starts in 1492 as the infobox does. The Mughal page for Aurangzeb's 1657 capture of Bidar (from Bijapur) is not opened here; see bijapur-sultanate.
